newsitem.title: USA: FGIC says has $15.5 mln annual exposure to Miami.
newsitem.headline: FGIC says has $15.5 mln annual exposure to Miami.

text.p: Financial Guaranty Insurance Co, unit of GE Capital Services, said Friday it has an average annual debt service exposure to Miami of $15.5 million.
The bond insurance company said it insured a total of $199.2 million of bonds for the Miami, which is facing a severe fiscal crisis and a budget deficit of $68 million.
FGIC said it insured $116.5 million in general obligation Miami bonds and $82.7 million in non-advalorem debt. Annual debt service on each amounts to $9.6 million and $5.9 million, respectively.
FGIC noted that Miami can only declare bankruptcy after getting the approval of Florida's governor. No such request has been made.

"We expect that officials of the state and city will move expeditiously to resolve these financial matters," the company said. FGIC said it has also met with state officials, who invited FGIC's input in drafting agreements on the dimensions of a state oversight panel for Miami.
GE Capital is a unit of General Electric Co.
